validationNotes:
First staging verification rejected an old dev-runtime CSS file with mixed line endings.
The exact current source file was copied atomically; all 3310 source hashes then matched.
The five runtime files in the release patch exactly match the full Linux tested source.
Only benchmark drivers, browser scripts, replay whitespace and documentation changed later.

Linux full: 2355 total, 2354 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip. The replay ran concurrently under
separate quotas, so its CPU timings are not a controlled isolated comparison.
Replay exact state hashes and byte counts are deterministic and equal across repeats.

First PostgreSQL load ended before any phase with PG_OPERATION_FAILED. It is retained
as a failed run, not a capacity result. Subsequent diagnostic reads of the isolated
schema and worker-open succeeded; the original low-level cause was not established.

Second load used a driver which still expected object player rows. v10 movement
snapshots arrived, but spawnSerial was not read and boosters were rejected correctly.
That run is excluded from capacity assessment. The benchmark driver now decodes only
its own player row using the shared decoder. Browser decoding was already correct.
Only subsequent validated runs qualify, with all 30 booster types and ACK/PG/WAL checks.

One SSH request lost its connection before the handshake; retry succeeded without a
service restart. A replay fixture whitespace check was fixed in a follow-up commit.
Negative runs and evidence are preserved. No production gameplay data was used in load.
Deployment preflight refused an already existing RAM staging name used by the first load. It stopped before maintenance/service changes. Backup staging was given a separate unused path; no test evidence was deleted.
The first 40-second startup readiness window expired while the cold full-world read was still running. The service remained active with zero restarts; entry stayed closed until a subsequent readiness and full readback check.
remaining: Addressed profile commits and separate history storage

30–60 minute and 6–24 hour load soaks on a separate test host
Client FPS on real low-end devices
